lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPower_const_cost
lean.annotation: Appendix G.4 reports about 12.8 times fewer walk steps and 1.30 times fewer logical qubits, despite about 1.42 times as many T gates per step. Those rounded factors explain the scale of the reported 11.8-fold reduction against the baseline estimate; the Lean cost theorem bounds the solution side only.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPowerConstCost
lean.annotation: Dividing the proved cap by 500 gives $4.5872\times10^{14}$ per run. Appendix G.2 gives about $5.42\times10^{15}$ per run for the reconstructed baseline. Dividing the latter by the former gives about $11.8$.
